source: Brewer and Treyens (1981) Role of schemata in memory for places (checked via secondary pages only)
finding: Original paper is paywalled (Semantic Scholar: closed access, 833 citations) and the Scribd copy would not render. Two secondary pages were read. They agree on direction: schema-expected items (books, lamp, window) were falsely recalled or recognised, the skull was remembered poorly, schema expectancy correlated positively with memory while saliency barely did.
numbers: No intrusion rates or recognition rates could be verified. Sample size conflicts: one educational page says 86 participants and 35 seconds in the office; other summaries say 30. They may refer to different experiments. Do not cite either as the main N.
limits: Secondary sources only, so opened is false for the primary. Gap 1 stays open.
agent_relevance: Treat the office study as qualitative support for schema intrusion. Do not quote rates.

source: Bergman and Roediger (1999) Can Bartlett's repeated reproduction experiments be replicated? Memory and Cognition 27
finding: Abstract page read (full text paywalled). Authors say earlier partial replications failed, so they ran a close copy of Bartlett: study The War of the Ghosts, test at 15 min, again at 1 week, and at 6 months for as many people as could be found. They report that people forgot the story, added rationalisation and distortion, that the share of distorted material rose with delay, and that new propositions were imported at long delay.
numbers: Delays 15 min, 1 week, 6 months. No N, rates or effect sizes could be read (abstract only).
quote: Bartlett's repeated reproduction results can be replicated.
limits: Abstract only. It rejects the claim that Bartlett cannot be replicated, but effect size is unknown here. It is repeated reproduction, so people also rehearse the story.
agent_relevance: Distortion grows with delay in humans, so the agent analogue is delay across rewrites, not one recall.

source: Rojahn and Pettigrew (1992) Memory for schema-relevant information: a meta-analytic resolution. British Journal of Social Psychology 31
finding: Meta-analysis of person-memory studies. Overall a slight memory advantage for schema-inconsistent information. Effects are heterogeneous. Direction depends on the memory measure: recall and recognition corrected for guessing favour inconsistent items; recognition uncorrected for guessing favours consistent items. Moderators: processing demands, exposure time, delay, proportion of inconsistent items, degree of inconsistency.
numbers: 60 independent studies, 165 comparative tests. Pooled effect size is not in the abstract. The abstract compares itself with a similar meta-analysis (Stangor and McMillan 1992), not opened.
limits: Abstract only. Person-memory (social schema) studies up to 1992. No newer meta-analysis was found in this pass.
agent_relevance: Explains the mixed human results on congruent versus incongruent items. Score note recall with a guessing correction.

source: Acerbi and Stubbersfield (2023) Large language models show human-like content biases in transmission chain experiments. PNAS 120
finding: Five preregistered transmission-chain experiments with ChatGPT (GPT-3 era) using human study material. It kept stereotype-consistent over stereotype-inconsistent content, negative over positive, social over non-social, threat-related over neutral. Ambiguous details were mostly resolved negatively.
numbers: Mixed-model coefficients, all P<0.01 or smaller: stereotype consistent 0.058; negative 0.117; ambiguity resolved negatively 0.183; social 0.321; threat 0.523 (negative vs neutral 0.070); mixed biases 0.076. Each result averages five replications.
limits: Older model, short chains, outcome is proportion of content retained. Gender-stereotype consistency is the closest match to schema-congruent gap keeping. Surprise or novelty was not tested directly.
agent_relevance: When the agent summarises notes, expect it to keep stereotype-fitting, negative and threat content and resolve ambiguity negatively. Log ambiguous items instead of resolving them.

source: Perez et al. (2025, ICLR) When LLMs play the telephone game (re-read for design details)
finding: Chains of LLM agents rewrote text for 50 generations. Less constrained tasks (take inspiration, continue) drift more than the constrained rephrase task. Toxicity converges fast to a narrow peak near zero. Positivity is partly kept under rephrase. Length rises for some models (GPT-4o-mini, Mixtral) and falls for others (GPT-3.5, Llama3-8B).
numbers: 6 models x 3 tasks x 20 initial texts x 5 seeds x 50 steps, so 100 chains per model-task cell. KS tests against generation 1: p-values fall with generation in most cells, more often for open tasks. A 100-text replication is in the appendix.
limits: Measures toxicity, positivity, difficulty and length, not facts. Chains used one model each. No provenance or source-tag condition. 50 steps is far longer than a normal note rewrite count.
agent_relevance: Gap 9 partly answered: drift is visible by tens of rewrites even for rephrase, but its size at 3 to 10 rewrites is not reported. Keep rewrites constrained and rare.

source: Kumar, Marjieh et al. (2024) multimodal serial reproduction (re-read for N)
finding: Humans and GPT-4 reproduced 8x8 binary boards through image or language. Adding language as a bottleneck changed human chains more than GPT-4 chains, so GPT-4 seems to use language representations even for visual input.
numbers: 348 human participants (Prolific), chains of 10 iterations. Multimodal chains had higher velocity than unimodal: human t(198)=4.05, p<0.0001; GPT-4 t(198)=-7.01, p<0.0001 (opposite sign).
limits: Abstract grids, not stories, so it does not test Bartlett-style rationalisation. It is the closest LLM serial reproduction study found.
agent_relevance: No LLM study of Bartlett-style story recall was found; this neighbour is about abstraction, not distortion.

source: Chan et al. (2024) Conversational AI powered by LLMs amplifies false memories in witness interviews
finding: Human witnesses of a crime video were asked five misleading questions by a survey, a scripted chatbot or a generative LLM chatbot. The LLM chatbot raised false memories most. After one week the count held, and confidence in false memories stayed above control.
numbers: N=200, four conditions. Immediate false memories more than 3x control and 1.7x survey. 36.4% of responses to the generative chatbot were misled.
limits: This is LLM-caused false memory in people, not LLM memory. Link to schema is only through suggested expected details.
agent_relevance: Leading questions in our own prompts can plant expected details in a reader. Avoid suggestive follow-ups when asking the agent to recall.

source: Wu et al. (2024) Reasoning or reciting? Counterfactual tasks (re-read for the comprehension-check design)
finding: 11 task pairs with default versus counterfactual rules (base-9 arithmetic, swapped indexing, altered chess rules). GPT-4, GPT-3.5, Claude and PaLM-2 are consistently worse on counterfactual versions. A counterfactual comprehension check shows models mostly understand the new rule, so the drop is not just misreading. Zero-shot chain-of-thought and up to 16 in-context examples shrink the gap but do not close it.
numbers: 11 tasks. Per-cell accuracy sits in appendix tables whose headers did not survive text extraction, so no figures are quoted.
limits: Nobody tested an explicit 'state the default assumptions' step, so gap 6 is not answered. The 16-shot plateau is the evidence that prompting alone does not remove the gap.
agent_relevance: Default-world schemas leak in even when the new rule is understood. An assumptions-listing step needs its own equal-token test.

source: Zhang et al. (2026, ICLR) Agentic Context Engineering (ACE): context collapse
finding: When an LLM rewrites the whole accumulated context each step, the context can collapse into a short, less informative summary and accuracy falls below the no-context baseline. ACE avoids this with incremental delta edits and non-LLM merging.
numbers: AppWorld case with Dynamic Cheatsheet: step 60 had 18,282 tokens and 66.7 accuracy; the next step had 122 tokens and 57.1 accuracy; no-adaptation baseline 63.7.
limits: One observed case, not a measured rate. Whole-context rewriting is the worst case. ACE reports +10.6% on agents over baselines.
agent_relevance: Supports appending small notes and never asking the model to rewrite all memory in one step. Gap 9 at agent scale: collapse can happen in a single step.

source: Zhang et al. (2026, ICLR) ACE appendix A.4: harmful reflector injected into the playbook
finding: A reflector was told to inject harmful or conflicting bullets into the evolving playbook every X steps. Accuracy stayed above the base model unless the harmful update happened at every step.
limits: One benchmark, one model (DeepSeek-V3.1). Seeded wrong bullets sit inside abstraction-style memory. There is no raw-fact arm at equal tokens, so gap 2 is not settled.
agent_relevance: Seeded wrong rules cost little when rare (0.1 to 2.2 points) and a lot when constant. Clean updates dilute them.

source: Nakayashiki (2026) When stale constraints go unchecked: budgeted verification failures in inherited agent memory
finding: Provenance links existed, yet agents with a budget of two checks out of six rarely inspected the path behind a constraint that read as settled. When the source record had since withdrawn the constraint, they followed the stale memory. Forcing one slot onto the critical path removed most errors. A one-sentence target-blind rule (prefer memories that state a limit on a candidate direction) recovered the effect in one store.
numbers: 16 models. Path inspected in 20.1% and 23.1% of episodes with the constraint stated, 66.9% and 72.9% with it removed. Stale-consistent decisions 77.3%, 74.7%, 74.7% in primary run, replication, held-out domain. Forced critical slot: +74.0, +72.7, +61.3 points; interleaved replication +80.7; 10 new models +62.0 (n=250). Target-blind rule +89.3 points in the 3-constraint store; a content-free freshness cue did not move allocation.
limits: Single author. Memory forms were installed, not learned. Six-memory scenarios. Not a schema study, but it measures the same thing: a settled-sounding conclusion blocks re-checking even when the derivation is reachable.
agent_relevance: Gap 3 evidence: keeping the derivation is not enough, the agent must be made to open it. Pair stored derivations with a rule that forces inspection of stated limits.

source: Xiong et al. (2025) How memory management impacts LLM agents: experience-following behavior
finding: Agents copy the output of retrieved memory records when the task input is similar. Wrong records are replayed and can be re-stored, so errors propagate. Strict evaluator-gated addition and history-based deletion beat unfiltered addition.
numbers: Correctness of retained vs deleted records under coarse evaluation (Table 4): EhrAgent 44.1 vs 36.3 (4o-mini), 49.1 vs 32.1 (4.1-mini), 54.8 vs 48.2 (4.1-mini-FT); CIC-IoT 78.9 vs 56.7, 72.2 vs 55.1, 86.6 vs 61.0.
limits: Raw experience records, not abstracted rules. No abstraction arm, so no schema versus fact comparison.
agent_relevance: Wrong raw records already persist and spread. For gap 2 the open question is whether abstraction makes this stronger. Gate additions on later outcome checks.

source: Dong et al. (2026) Memory injection attacks on LLM agents via query-only interaction (MINJA)
finding: An attacker who can only send queries gets malicious records stored in agent memory and later retrieved as demonstrations for other users.
numbers: Average injection success rate 98.2%, attack success rate 76.8%, across three agents and four victim-target pairs.
limits: Adversarial setting, not natural schema drift. It shows only that stored wrong records are used.
agent_relevance: A seeded wrong note is retrieved and obeyed most of the time in similarity-based memory. Source-tag every stored note.

source: Deng and Sinchaisri (2026) Stale, misattributed, or late: where personal memory fails before generation
finding: Most memory failures arise before generation. Without update resolution, superseded values appear in the prompt. Serving only the active value of a correctly keyed slot removes stale exposure. Assigning revisions to the right slot is the hard part.
numbers: 70.3% of prompts exposed a superseded value without update resolution. Open-domain merge recall on LongMemEval never above 0.062. Four LLM key assigners had higher key recall than a rule extractor but lower clean-retrieval rates.
limits: Abstract and introduction read only. Personal-fact memory, not schema abstraction.
agent_relevance: Tag notes with a slot key and validity so a correction replaces rather than sits beside the old value.

source: Chen, Wang and Brinton (2026) Fresh memory, stale plans: derivation currency (PlanFence)
finding: An agent can hold the latest requirement yet act on a plan derived from an older one. Storing exact links from a plan to the inputs it was derived from, and checking them before acting, fixes it.
numbers: Detected handoff conflicts rose from 0/30 to 30/30 when inherited input versions were supplied. In 30 live five-agent workflows with a revision after planning, a freshness-only executor acted on the stale plan every time (30/30); PlanFence completed all 30 correctly.
limits: Abstract and introduction read. Multi-agent handoff, application code supplies the links. No LLM summarisation involved.
agent_relevance: Direct support for storing the inputs a conclusion was derived from and re-checking them after a correction (gap 3), in a second task family.

source: Who Remembers What? Tracing information fidelity in human-AI chains (2025)
finding: Abstract only. 700 five-step transmission chains (human-only, LLM-only, mixed, cross-LLM) built on Bartlett serial reproduction and noisy-channel ideas. Hybrid chains are asymmetric: a human summary refined by an LLM tends to keep meaning well. New metrics: Information Degradation Rate, Meaning Preservation Entropy, Cascaded Hallucination Propagation Index.
numbers: 700 chains of 5 steps. No effect sizes in the abstract.
limits: Paper PDF and data repository could not be found; not read. Pointer for gaps 4 and 9 only.
agent_relevance: Five steps is the right scale for agent note chains. Find the full paper before relying on it.

source: Wynn and Logie (1998) The veracity of long-term memories; Gauld and Stephenson (1967)
finding: Only the Crossref bibliographic record for Wynn and Logie was reachable. The Wiley page is behind a bot wall and Gauld and Stephenson could not be retrieved. No numbers were read.
limits: Nothing may be cited from this line except that the papers exist. Gap 5 stays open.
agent_relevance: None until the papers are read.
